# blare

> Error alerting for Python and Node.js that needs no server, no database and no
> dashboard. It captures failures, groups identical ones into a single message, and
> posts that message to Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams or any webhook.
> One message per problem, not one per crash.

This file is written for coding agents. It is enough to install and wire blare into a
repository correctly without reading the source. Normative behaviour lives in SPEC.md.

- Source: https://github.com/D4RKGEEK/blare
- Spec (normative): https://github.com/D4RKGEEK/blare/blob/main/SPEC.md
- Conformance fixtures: https://github.com/D4RKGEEK/blare/tree/main/conformance
- License: Apache-2.0. No account, no API key, no telemetry, no hosted component.
- Current version: 0.1.0 (spec v1)

## Packages

| Runtime | Package | Install | Minimum |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Python | `blare` (PyPI) | `pip install blare` | 3.9 |
| Node / TypeScript | `@geekvb/blare` (npm) | `npm i @geekvb/blare` | 18 |

The names differ because npm's typosquatting filter refuses the unscoped name. Same
project, same spec version, same fixtures.

## The whole integration

1. Add the package to the dependency file (`pyproject.toml` / `requirements.txt`, or
   `package.json`). Do not vendor it.
2. Call `init()` **once**, at process start, before the first import or call that can
   fail. Not per request, not per worker, not lazily.
3. Register **exactly one** framework hook, chosen from what the dependency file
   actually contains. Adding two produces duplicate captures.
4. Set `BLARE_SINKS` in the environment. Put a placeholder in `.env.example` and in the
   deployment config. Never commit a real webhook URL, and never read `BLARE_SINKS` from
   application code.
5. Run the smoke test and show the output: `python -m blare --send` or
   `npx @geekvb/blare --send`.

### Python

```python
import blare
blare.init()
```

```python
# FastAPI, Starlette, Litestar, Quart — any ASGI app
from blare.integrations.asgi import BlareASGIMiddleware
app.add_middleware(BlareASGIMiddleware)

# Flask, Django, or any WSGI app
from blare.integrations.flask import install
install(app)

# Celery
from blare.integrations.celery import install as install_celery
install_celery(celery_app)
```

### Node / TypeScript

```js
import blare from "@geekvb/blare";
blare.init();
```

```js
// Express — after your routes, as the last middleware
import { blareErrorHandler } from "@geekvb/blare";
app.use(blareErrorHandler());

// Fastify
import { blarePlugin } from "@geekvb/blare";
app.register(blarePlugin);
```

## What is captured with no code change

`init()` alone installs these. Do **not** wrap application code in try/except or
try/catch merely to report an error — it is already captured.

| Source | Python | Node |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing log calls | `logging` handler on the root logger | pino stream, winston transport |
| Unhandled crashes | `sys.excepthook`, thread hook | `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection` |
| Web frameworks | FastAPI, Starlette, Litestar, Quart, Flask, Django, any WSGI | Express, Fastify, NestJS, Next.js (server) |
| Background jobs | Celery | — |
| Manual | `blare.capture(exc)` | `blare.capture(err)` |

## Configuration (environment variables only)

There is no config file and no init options worth passing.

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BLARE_SINKS` | — | Webhook URLs, comma separated. The only required one. |
| `BLARE_ENV` | `unknown` | Shown on every alert, e.g. `production`. |
| `BLARE_SERVICE` | derived | Service name on the alert. |
| `BLARE_LEVEL` | `ERROR` | Minimum level that alerts. |
| `BLARE_DEDUPE_WINDOW` | `300` | Seconds of silence per fingerprint. |
| `BLARE_MAX_PER_HOUR` | `20` | Hard ceiling across all problems; `0` disables. |
| `BLARE_IGNORE` | — | Glob patterns dropped before anything else. |
| `BLARE_STATE` | `file` | `memory`, `file`, or `redis://…` for multi-host dedupe. |
| `BLARE_DRY_RUN` | `false` | Render to stderr, send nothing. |
| `BLARE_ENABLED` | `true` | The off switch. |

Destination format is detected from the webhook hostname: `hooks.slack.com` gives Block
Kit, `discord.com` gives an embed, `*.webhook.office.com` gives an Adaptive Card or the
legacy MessageCard, and anything else receives the canonical event as JSON. There is no
scheme or per-service setting to choose.

## Behaviour an agent should not re-implement

- **Fingerprint** = exception type + the innermost stack frame that is *not* in
  `site-packages` or `node_modules` + the message with variable parts (numbers, UUIDs,
  hex, emails, URLs, paths, quoted strings) replaced. Identical across hosts, processes,
  and both language ports.
- **Throttle** = one alert per fingerprint per `BLARE_DEDUPE_WINDOW`, plus a hard
  `BLARE_MAX_PER_HOUR` ceiling. Suppressed occurrences are not lost; they ride along as a
  count on the next alert, so there is no background timer and no second summary message.
- **State** is a lock-guarded file in the OS temp directory by default, shared by every
  process on the host, so four workers seeing one crash send one alert.
- **Redaction** runs after fingerprinting (so a rule change cannot regroup history) and
  before rendering (so no sink sees a raw value). Locals, request and response bodies,
  query strings and environment variable values are never collected at all.
- **Delivery** happens on a worker thread behind a bounded queue, retries twice, and
  never raises into the application. If the queue fills, alerts are dropped and counted
  rather than back-pressuring production traffic.

## Out of scope — do not build these on top

blare has no history, search, dashboard, metrics, traces or uptime checks, and it does not
notify end users. If the task needs any of those, the answer is an error tracker (Sentry,
GlitchTip, Bugsink) alongside blare, not an extension to it. There is no browser support:
a webhook URL in frontend JavaScript is a public secret.

## Definition of done

The app still starts; exactly one `init()` call and one framework hook exist; `BLARE_SINKS`
and `BLARE_ENV` are documented as placeholders and set in the environment; no webhook URL
is in tracked code; existing logging calls are untouched; the smoke test posted one
message; and the diff is roughly fifteen lines plus the dependency entry.
